feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It shows breadth and progression well, but impact could be sharper through more quantified outcomes, and the document feels slightly dense/redundant across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital/platform leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo with visible progression, enterprise-scale web work, and relevant tools/platforms.  
- Good specificity: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well but could better show results (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement growth, cost savings, adoption improvements).  
- Fix style consistency: use parallel bullet structure throughout; standardize punctuation around lists and compounds (e.g., “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”). “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler for education. No major misspellings found, but there are minor stylistic inconsistencies in hyphenation and list formatting.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It would be sharper with a few concrete signals of scope and less overlap with the subtitle, competencies, and work history.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and add scale: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel, more direct construction: “Specializes in enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider adding one high-impact qualifier from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” if space allows.
- Style fix: use “years’ experience” and keep hyphenation consistent (“mission-driven,” “AI-enabled,” “public-sector”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely repeats Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level or add scale instead of another skills list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned in style.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper phrases and keep each item parallel in structure.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Replace broader wording like “multi-channel communications operations” with more specific leadership language.
- Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this section or the Topline Skills categories.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” echoes multiple experience bullets; keep only if targeting public-sector or association roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and consistent style: “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched.”
- Clarify impact where possible: e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery,” “to support ongoing campaign expansion,” “for conference engagement.”
- Standardize wording and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series closely overlap with current and NACo role bullets; keep only if framed as standout examples rather than restating duties.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” feels most distinct—consider prioritizing it if space is tight.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 outcomes-led bullets and distinguish it from your NACo leadership role by emphasizing hands-on consulting, platform delivery, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Combine overlapping bullets into outcome-focused lines, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Designed digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, publishers, campaigns launched, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, or engagement improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep this version more implementation-focused.
- The AI search and microsite bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level and let projects hold specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and operational scale.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements for reporting speed, production cost/time savings from the in-house studio, engagement growth, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten channel language: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available, or cut this bullet if no standout result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry’s newsletter/social/video operations.
- Video-programming language may duplicate both the earlier NACo role and Recent Projects unless this bullet emphasizes the studio build and operational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than ownership. Tighten it around scope, cadence, and operational impact to distinguish it from the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video point: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built tighter editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and speed of digital publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.
- “workflow/governance improvements” overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role; keep this entry focused on day-to-day operations and coordination.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrases like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, higher-level terms tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Content strategy for complex, high-volume organizations
- Consider “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect governance, workflows, and scale.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this skill group to outcomes already shown in experience (10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than adding vague descriptors here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, with less low-level detail.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as capability-led, not platform-led: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation for public-sector web platforms • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- De-emphasize older/basic terms like “jQuery” unless required for target roles; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” can become “front-end implementation” for a more senior tone.
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “for high-volume, multi-publisher websites” or “for enterprise public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost verbatim; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve specific tools there.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear elsewhere; avoid repeating identical phrasing across sections.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value proposition. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Group tools more tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool inventory there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; combine if space is tight.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Make it more senior, operational, and aligned to recent leadership in building NACo’s in-house studio and event capability.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Tighten and elevate the bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and studio system operations  
- Virtual event delivery and technical coordination
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase instead of a fifth tool item, e.g. **Built in-house studio capability for recurring advocacy and event programming**
- Keep wording consistent with other topline skills by using noun phrases, not mixed verb/tool formats.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the NACo role bullet about building the in-house studio; avoid repeating that exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly. Use this space to signal depth and recency, with Drupal clearly leading.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10, enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, swap GitHub Pages for a stronger capability label: **Static site publishing** or **Headless/static publishing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-specific.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid overemphasizing it elsewhere without adding context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** HTML • CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value and date the section.
- Consider replacing **jQuery** with **JavaScript/jQuery** only if it is still actively used in recent work; otherwise remove it to keep the list modern.
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end troubleshooting**, **deployment workflows**, or **serverless scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “API integrations” and broader technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies and recent work bullets.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. **Used to build editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team coordination workflows**
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier are the real automation stack, keep them prominent and consider dropping one lower-value PM tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are standard collaboration tools and may dilute the section unless they support a broader workflow-systems framing

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and underplays your stronger recent leadership in email operations. It should signal scale and use context from NACo without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Higher Logic (newsletter and member communications operations)** or **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation)**
- Keep platform names concise; avoid slashes if possible for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused, not outcome-focused.
- “Multi-channel communications” already appears elsewhere, so avoid adding broad channel language here.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” It should either be tightened to a sharper tools list or reframed to emphasize optimization methods/outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboards”
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO” to make the skill more concrete and tool/method specific.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI dashboards” or “executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in recent roles instead of listing broadly, e.g., “Built analytics/reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly a duplicate of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider removing one or making this section tools-only and the topline section outcomes-focused.
- “A/B testing” and “SEO” are methods, while the rest are platforms; mixing categories makes the list feel less precise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it around foundational impact and early leadership, and add scale/results if available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, for member and advocacy communications.”
- Sharpen leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; frame this as launching or establishing the format.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you specify this was the initial build-out phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes so it adds value without repeating later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Elevate the strongest achievement into a clear impact statement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger, higher-level multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, while letting work experience carry the impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
- Replace with a cleaner, tool-focused line: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast editing and production**
- Keep phrasing parallel: use either all software/tools or all capability labels; avoid mixing brand names with broad functions inconsistently.
- If accurate, add one higher-value production platform/tool instead of a generic phrase (e.g., streaming encoder/switcher, audio console, PTZ systems) to make this more concrete.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with **Multimedia production and livestream operations** and **Hybrid and virtual event production**; consider shortening here to just the tool/environment.
- “Podcast production” is already evidenced in older experience, so don’t over-expand it unless it remains a current strength.
